summary: This is the first lecture to enter the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, after five background episodes. The ustaz covers the marriage of Abdullah and Aminah, Abdullah's death while the Prophet was still in the womb, and what is certain about the birth: it was a Monday, in the Year of the Elephant, which is why fasting on Mondays is a sunnah. The exact date is uncertain, with about ten opinions. He explains how 12 Rabi' al-Awwal became the popular choice, where the maulid celebration came from, and urges us to focus on what is productive. He then tells of those who welcomed the newborn, how Abdul Muttalib named him Muhammad, and the social impact of naming children. He closes by stressing that unsourced miraculous birth stories are not needed for faith, because the Prophet ﷺ was a human being who received revelation.
keyPoints: What is certain about the Prophet's ﷺ birth is that he was born on a Monday, in the Year of the Elephant.
The Prophet ﷺ fasted on Mondays because that was the day he was born and the day he received the first revelation.
The exact birth date is uncertain because nothing was recorded; there are about ten opinions, and 12 Rabi' al-Awwal was chosen by Ibn Ishaq without a chain of narration.
The Prophet never mentioned his birth date or told anyone to do anything on that date, so arguing over it brings no benefit.
Abdul Muttalib named him Muhammad, and Umm Ayman, Thuwaybah and Abdul Muttalib were among the first to welcome him.
Names have a social impact: choose a good name, protect lineage, and avoid names that praise oneself or imitate those opposed to Islam.
Unsourced miraculous birth stories are not needed; the Prophet ﷺ was a human being who received revelation.

chapters.title: Opening and the virtue of knowledge gatherings
chapters.summary: The ustaz opens with a hadith about tranquillity and forgiveness in gatherings of knowledge.

chapters.title: Entering the Prophet's life through social impact
chapters.summary: After five background episodes, the lecture now enters the Prophet's ﷺ life, looking at the facts and their social impact.

chapters.title: The marriage of Abdullah and Aminah
chapters.summary: The marriage took place after Abdullah was saved from sacrifice; their exact ages are not known.

chapters.title: Reading the sirah in its own time
chapters.summary: The ustaz stresses that the sirah must not be judged by today's realities, including the age of marriage back then.

chapters.title: Hamzah and Umm Ayman
chapters.summary: Abdul Muttalib married Hala, the mother of Hamzah RA; Abdullah bought Umm Ayman, who stayed with the Prophet.

chapters.title: The death of Abdullah
chapters.summary: Abdullah died in Yathrib when the Prophet was two months in the womb, before the Year of the Elephant event according to the stronger narration.

chapters.title: Aminah's pregnancy
chapters.summary: Aminah had an unusually easy pregnancy, with feelings of both sadness and excitement.

chapters.title: What is certain: Monday
chapters.summary: A sahih hadith in Muslim says the Prophet fasted on Mondays because it was the day he was born and received revelation.

chapters.title: The Year of the Elephant and the influence of one's birth year
chapters.summary: The Arabs marked years by major events; the ustaz shows how the climate of a birth year shapes a generation's character.

chapters.title: 12 Rabi' al-Awwal and other opinions
chapters.summary: The date is uncertain because nothing was recorded; 12 Rabi' al-Awwal is popular through Ibn Ishaq's choice and worldwide celebration.

chapters.title: No benefit in arguing, and the Hijri calendar
chapters.summary: The Prophet never mentioned his birth date; Umar al-Khattab chose the Hijra, not the birth, as the start of the calendar.

chapters.title: Origin of the maulid celebration
chapters.summary: The ustaz recounts that the celebration began about five hundred years after the Prophet's death under the Fatimid dynasty, then spread.

chapters.title: Attitude towards the celebration
chapters.summary: The Prophet did not call for it; lectures and readings that do not contradict the Shariah are beneficial, but the priority is spreading the message.

chapters.title: Those who welcomed him, and the name Muhammad
chapters.summary: The Prophet was welcomed by Umm Ayman, nursed by Thuwaybah, and named Muhammad by Abdul Muttalib.

chapters.title: The social impact of naming
chapters.summary: Names shape character and fate; the ustaz explains guidance on choosing, changing and protecting a name.

chapters.title: Miraculous birth stories and conclusion
chapters.summary: Famous stories such as the collapse of the Persian palace have unclear sources; the ustaz sums up what is certain and the matter of naming.

books.context: The earliest sirah besides the Quran, hadith and the records of the Companions' children; Ibn Ishaq chose 12 Rabi' al-Awwal without giving a chain or reference.
A major reference that chooses 9 Rabi' al-Awwal based on calculations by astronomers.
Its introduction says that after the Prophet's death the Companions dispersed to spread the message, rather than weeping at his grave.
Cited for the idea that how we handle money is shaped by the year and era we were born in.
Source of the hadith on Monday fasting and the Prophet's birth.
books.note: Author not named in the lecture: Imam Muslim

books.context: Source of the hadith on Al-Abbas's dream about Abu Lahab.
books.note: Author not named in the lecture: Imam Bukhari

books.context: A summary and arrangement of Ibn Ishaq's sirah, explaining the Prophet's ﷺ birth and family.
Discusses the Prophet's ﷺ guidance, including birth and the naming of children.

people.context: Married after being saved from sacrifice; died in Yathrib when the Prophet was two months in the womb.
Arranged Abdullah's marriage, received news of the birth with joy, and named him Muhammad.
Had an unusually easy pregnancy and nursed the Prophet on the first and second days.
Aminah's cousin and the mother of Hamzah RA.

people.role: Uncle and milk-brother of the Prophet ﷺ
people.context: The Prophet's uncle, second cousin and milk-brother; the story of how he unexpectedly accepted Islam will be told later.

people.role: Abdullah's slave who cared for the Prophet
people.context: Bought by Abdullah and given to Aminah; present from before the Prophet's birth until after his death, and according to some sirah writers the first person to touch the Prophet at birth.
Chose 12 Rabi' al-Awwal without a chain or reference.
Chose 9 Rabi' al-Awwal based on astronomers' calculations.
Rejected the Prophet's birth year as the start of the Islamic calendar and chose the Hijra.
Mentions in Fiqh as-Sirah that the Companions dispersed to spread the message.

people.role: Abu Lahab's slave and the Prophet's wet nurse
people.context: Brought news of the birth to Abu Lahab and nursed the Prophet after Aminah.
Was glad at the Prophet's birth and freed Thuwaybah, though he later reviled the Prophet until Allah rebuked him.
Is said to have dreamed about Abu Lahab in a disputed hadith.

lessons.title: Read the sirah in its own time
lessons.body: The sirah must not be viewed through today's realities; we need to understand the context of the time, including the age of marriage.

lessons.title: The era of our birth shapes a generation's character
lessons.body: Events at the time we are born and grow up shape how a generation thinks and what it believes.

lessons.title: Weigh the atmosphere children grow up in
lessons.body: We need to assess today's atmosphere because it shapes how children approach life.

lessons.title: The birth date does not affect creed
lessons.body: The Prophet never mentioned his birth date or told anyone to do anything on it, so disagreement about it does not touch the pillars of belief.

lessons.title: Don't spend energy on lesser matters
lessons.body: A great deal of time and resources goes into things that are not really important.

lessons.title: Focus on the productive amid disagreement
lessons.body: Rather than heated argument over whether to celebrate, focus on what is more productive.

lessons.title: Lectures and readings that don't contradict the Shariah
lessons.body: Lectures, reading hadith and the Prophet's shama'il are beneficial and should continue all year, not only on a particular day.

lessons.title: The Companions spread the message
lessons.body: The Companions dispersed because they understood the essence of the Prophet's message: inviting people to know the Prophet and worship Allah.

lessons.title: Don't exaggerate in praising the Prophet
lessons.body: The Prophet warned against becoming like the Christians, who raised a prophet to be the son of God.

lessons.title: Give your children good names
lessons.body: A name matters because on the Day of Judgement we will be called by our own name and our father's name.

lessons.title: Protect lineage: change your own name, not your father's
lessons.body: When changing a name, change only your own so that your lineage can still be traced.

lessons.title: A name need not be Arabic, but must mean something good
lessons.body: The ustaz favours the view that a name need not come from the Arabic language as long as its meaning is good.

lessons.title: Avoid names that sanctify oneself or imitate the opposed
lessons.body: The Prophet forbade names that exalt or purify oneself, and names that praise people opposed to Islam.

lessons.title: Miraculous stories are not needed for faith
lessons.body: We can fully believe in prophethood without unsourced miraculous stories, and the Prophet was a human being who received revelation.

glossary.meaning: The year the elephant army attacked the Kaaba, and the year the Prophet ﷺ was born; the Arabs marked years by major events.
The celebration of the Prophet's ﷺ birthday.
A dynasty in Egypt with Shia doctrine, known for holding many celebrations.
The traits and character of the Prophet ﷺ.
The chain of narrators of a report.
Lineage; it must be protected because it lets a child be traced.
A sacrifice made to mark the birth of a child.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions it in the opening of the lecture.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said that in gatherings of knowledge, tranquillity descends and the sins of those present are forgiven, and whoever walks to attend a gathering of knowledge, Allah will ease his path to Paradise.

dalil.context: The ustaz says Allah values the sacrifice of a mother who bears hardship upon hardship in pregnancy and childbirth. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: We have commanded man to be good to his parents: his mother struggled to carry him and struggled to give birth to him- his bearing and weaning took a full thirty months. When he has grown to manhood and reached the age of forty he [may] say, ‘Lord, help me to be truly grateful for Your favours to me and to my parents; help me to do good work that pleases You; make my offspring good. I turn to You; I am one of those who devote themselves to You.’

dalil.context: The ustaz says this is certain because the hadith is sahih, and the sunnah is to fast and rejoice on Mondays.
dalil.translation: A Bedouin asked the Prophet ﷺ why he fasted on Mondays. He replied that it was the day he was born and the day he was appointed to receive the first revelation.

dalil.context: The ustaz says historians and sirah scholars agree that the birth year was the Year of the Elephant.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said that he was born in the Year of the Elephant.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions this while criticising expressions or poems that the Prophet himself did not allow.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ was very careful about being praised and exalted, and warned against becoming like the Christians, who raised a prophet to be the son of God.

dalil.context: The ustaz says this hadith is in Sahih Bukhari but disputed; some scholars take it as evidence, others reject that understanding. It is mentioned as information only, with no general recommendation drawn from it.
dalil.translation: Abu Lahab freed Thuwaybah out of joy at the birth of the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Abbas later dreamed that in the Fire, Abu Lahab was given relief on Mondays because of that joy.

dalil.context: The ustaz says its chain is good, and concludes that names matter and one's father's name should not be changed.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said that on the Day of Judgement you will be called by your names and your fathers' names, so make your names good.

dalil.context: Mentioned while discussing guidance on choosing names, which also encourages the names of the prophets.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said that the best names are Abdullah and Abdurrahman.

dalil.context: The ustaz says names that purify oneself are forbidden, and the Prophet also changed Asiyah to Jamilah and Huzn to Sahl; the family that refused to change the name Huzn is said to have remained in grief.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ forbade naming a girl Barrah, saying do not claim purity for yourselves, for Allah knows best who is righteous among you, and suggested the name Zaynab.

dalil.context: The ustaz says this hadith is disputed, and scholars differ on whether it is literal or a vision; it cannot be settled, and it does not affect faith.
dalil.translation: When the Prophet ﷺ was born, his mother saw a light come out of her womb that lit up as far as Sham.

dalil.context: The Prophet ﷺ said he was a man like us who received revelation; the ustaz cites it to reject exaggerated reverence. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Say, ‘I am only a human being, like you, to whom it has been revealed that your God is One. Anyone who fears to meet his Lord should do good deeds and give no one a share in the worship due to his Lord.

sirah.era: The birth of the Prophet ﷺ in the Year of the Elephant, in Mecca
sirah.summary: This episode covers events around the Prophet's ﷺ birth: Abdullah's marriage and death, the day and year of birth, those who welcomed him, the naming by Abdul Muttalib, and the dispute over the date.

events.label: Marriage
events.title: Abdullah marries Aminah
events.desc: After Abdullah was ransomed with a hundred camels; their exact ages are not known.

events.label: Death
events.title: Abdullah dies in Yathrib
events.desc: The Prophet was still two months in the womb; Abdullah was buried in the Banu Najjar quarter.

events.label: Birth
events.title: The Prophet is born on a Monday
events.desc: A sahih hadith in Muslim states that the day of birth and of the first revelation was Monday.

events.label: Year
events.title: The Year of the Elephant
events.desc: According to the strongest narration, the Prophet was born about fifty days after the elephant army incident.

events.label: Welcome
events.title: Welcomed by Umm Ayman
events.desc: Besides Umm Ayman, Thuwaybah and a woman named Ashifah are mentioned in some sirah accounts.

events.label: Naming
events.title: Abdul Muttalib names him Muhammad
events.desc: Abdul Muttalib took the Prophet to the Kaaba, prayed, and named him Muhammad so that he would always be praised on earth and in the heavens.

events.label: Custom
events.title: Circumcised and given the aqiqah by Abdul Muttalib
events.desc: According to the sirah records, Abdul Muttalib circumcised, named and performed the aqiqah for the Prophet.
